rows: PR batches are independent per PR; worker batches per worker_state; discord per channel-window — embarrassingly parallel fan-out
workers return proposals; ONE writer appends serially after each mapLimit wave (the existing curator output pattern) — no concurrent appends
two parallel batches can propose the same learning — so corroboration/dedupe runs as a SECOND, serial pass after the fan-out (librarian at thinking=high over the merged proposals), never during it
no rate-limit knob exists in-repo; codex-lb is the throttle. Start jobs=8, watch, raise to 16
runtime is a per-process singleton with pool max 1 — each parallel call is its own session; per-session timeout via --agent-timeout-seconds
batches are idempotent (content-keyed proposal ids); a killed run re-runs only unfinished batches from the batch manifest

steps.text: Stage 1 — smoke (~1 h): one worker through kg-librarian-condense, one PR, one discord window; Ford hand-reads the ledger output; calibrate real minutes-per-call

Stage 2 — source fan-outs, separate CLI runs with batch manifests (resumable): discord distillate (~1 h) → past PRs (~2–4 h @ jobs=16) → worker history (~2–3 h; the 1,617 dead-transcript workers take the checkpoint path)
between sources: Ford samples ~20 random learnings; ugly miss rate → tune prompt, re-run that source (batches idempotent)
Stage 3 — serial corroboration pass over merged proposals, then graph rebuild: learnings index onto targets, boot-card pointers live
